requirements.requirement: bin/publish must accept a release directory and switch current so concurrent readers continuously see either the complete previous release or the complete new release.
requirements.summary: The installed publisher validates the directory and MANIFEST, creates a same-directory temporary symlink, and renames it over current. A bounded concurrent test performed 601 switches while four readers made 10,000 checks for link presence, readable expected target, MANIFEST, and index data; it reported zero errors. Publishing still worked after restart.

requirements.requirement: A release missing MANIFEST must be refused without changing the previous current target.
requirements.summary: The incomplete release was rejected with current unchanged in the main functional test, the pre-restart health check, and the post-restart recovery check.

requirements.requirement: Both staged valid releases must remain preserved and publication must permit rollback to either release.
requirements.summary: Both releases retained their MANIFEST and index files. Direct publication to releases/one and releases/two succeeded before and after restart, with the expected target and content observed each time.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on Alpine Linux 3.23.3 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts before and after the work and restart. The implementation uses available BusyBox/POSIX shell facilities and passed shell syntax and behavioral checks.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the node was observably unavailable during reboot, a different boot ID appeared afterward, and publisher behavior, current data, staged releases, rejection behavior, OS, and kernel recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently agree with the executor evidence.
limitations: The concurrency test was bounded to 10,000 reader iterations and verified the release artifacts present in this task (MANIFEST and index.txt), rather than exhaustively modeling every possible future release layout.
Failed-service collection was unsupported on this Alpine node, although post-restart reachability, publisher behavior, data, sockets, and package health were directly observed.
Requirement release-preservation-rollback cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unnecessary managed-system mutation was identified: replacing the publisher (cmd-f8936b78fca343ca), exercising publication (cmd-1b7c19b0feb7422b), restarting for the mandatory protocol (cmd-99c4b80c47414e2a), and post-restart publication checks (cmd-e0db9222be084cd8) each supported implementation or verification. However, four low-risk test artifacts were abandoned in /tmp: publish-reject.out and publish-reader-errors from cmd-1b7c19b0feb7422b, pre-reboot-reject.out from cmd-4ba3a9fc840241bf, and post-reboot-reject.out from cmd-e0db9222be084cd8. Package-health output was unchanged and no new exposure was observed; socket differences are consistent with the verified reboot.
